exposure: ATR-X syndrome (Alpha Thalassemia mental Retardation syndrome, X-linked)
cohort: The study included 22 individuals diagnosed with ATR-X syndrome, aged 2-68 years, with three deceased at the time of the study.
finding: The study provided detailed descriptions of the clinical phenotype of ATR-X syndrome, reporting a variable degree of intellectual disability, specific prevalence of alpha thalassemia (30%) and genital anomalies (70%), and frequent occurrence of various health and behavioral problems.
cross-section timing: Individuals were aged 2-68 years at the time of the study.
